sentence: This project builds machine learning tools that use electronic health record data to improve how sepsis progress is assessed and treatment is planned.
This project uses spinal cord imaging and functional assessments to predict outcomes after surgery for degenerative cervical myelopathy.
This project studies how triple-negative breast cancer cells cause immunosuppression in their tumor microenvironment.
This project studies how a cancer-controlled enzyme adds a chemical mark to boost proteins and metabolites that tumors need, and tests ways to block it.
This project produces molecular reagents, monitors cells, and supplies cell populations and nanobodies for work on immune cells that target cancer.
This project builds a model system to study stem cell dormancy, a state that preserves regenerative capacity.
This project uses rodent models to find out how gonadal hormones shape neural circuits for social approach and vigilance during adolescence.
This project studies how a G-protein coupled receptor boosts natural killer cells and uses it to improve cell therapy against cancer.
This project generates and analyzes omics data, including metagenomics, transcriptomics and metabolomics, and shares the data with other researchers.
This project builds a circuit design platform that uses epigenetic regulation to give mammalian cells memory and timed gene expression.
This project tests whether oncolytic viruses that target the tumor microenvironment and an immune checkpoint can help the immune system fight pancreatic cancer.
This project tests whether bi-steric inhibitors prevent translation of an mRNA that drives rhabdomyosarcoma, a soft tissue sarcoma of childhood.
This project builds a cloud-native pipeline and uses it to develop methods that predict adverse outcomes among lung cancer patients.
This project provides next-generation sequencing technologies and expertise in experimental design and analysis of sequence data for researchers.
This project studies the molecular signatures that gonadotropins produce during ovarian aging, using mouse and human aging models.
This project uses genetically modified miniature pigs to study how to induce immune tolerance so transplanted pig organs are not rejected.
This project uses deep learning to make fetal brain magnetic resonance imaging faster and less affected by motion.
This project creates single-cell maps of the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus by comparing tissues from humans and non-human primates across life stages.
This project studies how a repressor complex keeps antiviral genes off until viral infection, using human cells and knock out mouse models.
This project develops a web-based tool that uses MRI and finite-element methods to screen for risk of atypical femoral fracture.
